scenes.text: This smiling salamander can regrow its legs, parts of its heart, and even parts of its brain.
It's the axolotl, and it comes from the lakes around Mexico City.
Lose a limb, and an axolotl simply grows a new one.
It can also repair a damaged spinal cord.
And it heals without leaving permanent scars.
Scientists study it closely, hoping to learn how regeneration might one day help humans.
They become adults at about one year old, yet keep their baby features for life, which is called neoteny.
That's why they still have those feathery gills sprouting from their heads.
They also have lungs, and can even breathe through their skin.
They grow up to about twelve inches long, and can live ten to fifteen years in the wild.
But in the wild, they are critically endangered.
They now survive only in a few canals of Lake Xochimilco, near Mexico City.
One estimate says somewhere between fifty and one thousand are left in the wild.
If you could regrow one body part, which would you pick?

title: This animal can regrow parts of its brain 🦎
caption: Axolotls can regrow lost limbs, parts of their heart, spinal cord and brain without permanent scars. In the wild they're critically endangered. 🇲🇽
